answer: Peer prediction pays graders by comparing each grade to the panel aggregate under a proper scoring rule, so lazy grading earns zero while accurate grading compounds reputation and pay. Every identity stakes a walnut bond that grows on a spiral curve with reputation. A sybil cannot predict the panel, so misgrades are slashed to honest graders; each fake identity burns a fresh stake while adding no signal. The attacker ends up funding the lagoon of rewards instead of draining it, so sockpuppets are strictly unprofitable.
